questions.question: Explain Gandhi's method of satyagraha and its influence on resistance in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Gandhi in SA 1893-1914; Pietermaritzburg train incident; Natal Indian Congress 1894; Black Act 1906 (registration, fingerprints); satyagraha: openly, non-violently break unjust laws and accept punishment; marches, strikes, burning certificates, imprisonment; concessions 1914; India independent 1947. Legacy debated (campaigned for Indians, early prejudiced views). SAIC passive resistance 1946-48 (Dadoo, Naicker, over 2 000 arrested) inspired ANC; Manilal Gandhi defied in 1952.

questions.question: Describe the planning, events and results of the Defiance Campaign.
questions.expected_answer: Joint Planning Council 1951 (ANC + SAIC); demanded repeal of six laws by 29 Feb 1952 (pass laws, stock limitation, Group Areas, Separate Representation of Voters, Suppression of Communism, Bantu Authorities); Malan refused. Mandela volunteer-in-chief, Cachalia deputy; pledge of non-violence, no fines. Began 26 June 1952: Port Elizabeth station, Boksburg (Sisulu, Nana Sita), curfews, whites-only facilities, passes; strongest in Eastern Cape; over 8 000 arrested; all races (Patrick Duncan, Manilal Gandhi). Leaders convicted of statutory communism, suspended sentences. Riots late 1952 (not part of campaign). Public Safety Act and Criminal Law Amendment Act 1953 ended it. Results: no laws repealed; ANC about 7 000 to 100 000; African-Indian unity, SACPO and COD, Congress Alliance; new leaders; UN discussed apartheid 1952; Luthuli elected.

questions.question: Describe Albert Luthuli's life, leadership and ideas.
questions.expected_answer: Born about 1898; Groutville mission; teacher at Adams College; Christian lay preacher; elected chief of Groutville 1936; joined ANC 1944, Natal president 1951; refused to leave ANC, dismissed November 1952; "The Road to Freedom is via the Cross" (thirty years knocking on a closed door; non-violence; suffering); ANC President-General December 1952 to 1967; banned and confined, Treason Trial; non-racialism and non-violence; Congress Alliance; Nobel Peace Prize for 1960 (received 1961), first African; "Let My People Go" 1962; died July 1967 hit by a train.
